title: Principles for Federal Infrastructure Investments
summary: Executive Order 12893 establishes principles for federal infrastructure investment and requires each agency with infrastructure responsibilities to develop implementation plans. Agencies must submit initial plans to the Office of Management and Budget by March 15 1994, and the OMB will provide guidance. title: Identification of Trade Expansion Priorities

title: Enabling All Qualified Americans To Serve Their Country in Uniform
summary: Executive Order 14004 directs the Department of Defense and the Department of Homeland Security to remove barriers for transgender individuals to serve openly in the U.S. military and to correct related personnel records.

title: Ensuring the Future Is Made in All of America by All of America's Workers
summary: Executive Order 14005 establishes a Made‑in‑America Office within OMB to centralize waiver reviews and directs agencies to report and act on domestic‑preference procurement.

title: Reforming Our Incarceration System To Eliminate the Use of Privately Operated Criminal Detention Facilities
summary: The order directs the Attorney General not to renew DOJ contracts with privately operated criminal detention facilities, thereby limiting the federal government’s reliance on such facilities.

title: President's Council of Advisors on Science and Technology
summary: Executive Order 14007 establishes the President’s Council of Advisors on Science and Technology (PCAST) and sets a two‑year termination deadline for the council.

title: Tackling the Climate Crisis at Home and Abroad
summary: Executive Order 14008 creates multiple climate‑focused bodies (Special Presidential Envoy, White House Office of Domestic Climate Policy, National Climate Task Force, Interagency Working Group on Coal and Power Plant Communities, White House Environmental Justice Interagency Council, and Advisory Council), reinstates a 2016 Presidential Memorandum, and directs a wide range of agencies to develop plans, strategies, and reports on climate finance, security, action plans, conservation, and environmental‑justice metrics, many with specific deadlines ranging from 30 days to February 2022.

title: Strengthening Medicaid and the Affordable Care Act
summary: Executive Order 14009 directs the President’s administration to strengthen Medicaid and the Affordable Care Act. It directs the Secretary of Health and Human Services to consider a special enrollment period and requires the Treasury, Labor, Health and Human Services, and other agency heads to review existing regulations and actions for consistency with the order’s policy, and to suspend or rescind those that are inconsistent. The order also revokes Executive Orders 13765 and 13813, which had limited ACA provisions. The order is implemented consistent with applicable law and subject to appropriations.

title: Creating a Comprehensive Regional Framework To Address the Causes of Migration, To Manage Migration Throughout North and Central America, and To Provide Safe and Orderly Processing of Asylum Seekers at the United States Border
summary: Executive Order 14010 revokes several prior immigration‑related directives and sets time‑bound reporting and rule‑making requirements for the Department of Homeland Security and other agencies.

title: Establishment of Interagency Task Force on the Reunification of Families
summary: Executive Order 14011 creates an interagency task force to reunify families separated at the U.S.–Mexico border and sets reporting and termination timelines.

title: Restoring Faith in Our Legal Immigration Systems and Strengthening Integration and Inclusion Efforts for New Americans
summary: EO 14012 creates a Task Force on New Americans and a Naturalization Working Group, directs multiple agencies to develop plans and reports within specified timeframes (60‑180 days), and revokes the 2019 Presidential Memorandum on sponsor responsibilities.

title: Rebuilding and Enhancing Programs To Resettle Refugees and Planning for the Impact of Climate Change on Migration
summary: Executive Order 14013 revokes two prior refugee‑related executive orders and a 2017 Presidential Memorandum, and directs a series of agency reports, reviews and actions to rebuild and expand the U.S. Refugee Admissions Program (USRAP) and related Special Immigrant Visa (SIV) programs, as well as a climate‑change‑migration report.

title: Blocking Property With Respect to the Situation in Burma
summary: Executive Order 14014 blocks property and related transactions of designated persons connected to the Burmese military regime, prohibits contributions and entry of such persons, bans evasion activities, and authorizes the Treasury to implement the sanctions.

title: Establishment of the White House Office of Faith- Based and Neighborhood Partnerships
summary: Executive Order 14015 creates the White House Office of Faith‑Based and Neighborhood Partnerships, directs it to begin operations within 30 days, and outlines its functions.

title: Revocation of Executive Order 13801
summary: Executive Order 14016 revokes Executive Order 13801, which had expanded apprenticeships.

title: America's Supply Chains
summary: Executive Order 14017 establishes a coordinated inter‑agency process and a series of time‑bound reporting requirements to strengthen the resilience of U.S. supply chains.

title: Revocation of Certain Presidential Actions
summary: Executive Order 14018 revokes a series of prior executive orders, memoranda, and related presidential actions.

title: Promoting Access to Voting
summary: Executive Order 14019 creates an interagency steering group on Native American voting rights and directs multiple agencies to develop plans and reports on voting‑access initiatives.

title: Establishment of the White House Gender Policy Council
summary: Executive Order 14020 creates the White House Gender Policy Council and directs it to coordinate federal actions on gender equity, set deadlines for staffing and strategy development, and terminates/amends a prior working group.
topic_other_reason: the order’s substantive focus is gender equity and equality policy

title: Guaranteeing an Educational Environment Free From Discrimination on the Basis of Sex, Including Sexual Orientation or Gender Identity
summary: Executive Order 14021 directs the Secretary of Education, in consultation with the Attorney General, to review and report on all federal‑assisted education agency actions that conflict with the policy guaranteeing students an environment free from sex‑based discrimination, including sexual orientation and gender identity. Within 100 days the Secretary must provide findings to the OMB Director and may issue new guidance, consider revising or rescinding inconsistent rules, and pursue additional enforcement actions.

title: Termination of Emergency With Respect to the International Criminal Court
summary: Executive Order 14022 terminates the national emergency that was created by EO 13928 and revokes that earlier order.

title: Establishment of the Presidential Commission on the Supreme Court of the United States
summary: Executive Order 14023 creates the Presidential Commission on the Supreme Court of the United States, a body focused on Supreme Court reform.

title: Blocking Property With Respect To Specified Harmful Foreign Activities of the Government of the Russian Federation
summary: Executive Order 14024 blocks property and suspends entry for persons linked to specified harmful activities of the Russian government.

title: Worker Organizing and Empowerment
summary: Executive Order 14025 establishes a Task Force on Worker Organizing and Empowerment, revokes two prior orders, and sets a 180‑day deadline for the Task Force to submit recommendations.

title: Increasing the Minimum Wage for Federal Contractors
summary: Executive Order 14026 sets new minimum‑wage requirements for federal contractors and directs agencies to implement them through regulations and FAR amendments. It also revokes EO 13838 and supersedes EO 13658.
instrument_other_reason: establishes a minimum‑wage policy for contractors – not covered by the listed instrument categories

title: Establishment of the Climate Change Support Office
summary: Executive Order 14027 creates the Climate Change Support Office within the Department of State.

title: Improving the Nation's Cybersecurity
summary: Key actions in Executive Order 14028 (Improving the Nation's Cybersecurity)

title: Revocation of Certain Presidential Actions and Technical Amendment
summary: The order revokes a series of prior presidential actions and, through a technical amendment, revokes EO 13957 and amends Civil Service Rule VI to eliminate Schedule F in the excepted service.

title: Climate-Related Financial Risk
summary: Executive Order 14030 directs multiple agencies to develop strategies, issue reports, and take actions on climate‑related financial risk, and it reinstates a previously revoked flood‑risk standard.

title: Advancing Equity, Justice, and Opportunity for Asian Americans, Native Hawaiians, and Pacific Islanders
summary: Executive Order 14031 establishes the President’s Advisory Commission on Asian Americans, Native Hawaiians, and Pacific Islanders and the White House Initiative on Asian Americans, Native Hawaiians, and Pacific Islanders; directs HHS to fund and support the Commission; requires each Initiative agency to prepare a plan; mandates an annual interagency report; and sets the Commission’s termination two years after the order unless renewed.

title: Addressing the Threat From Securities Investments That Finance Certain Companies of the People's Republic of China
summary: Executive Order 14032 expands the national emergency on securities investments that finance certain Chinese companies. It prohibits U.S. persons from purchasing or selling publicly traded securities of listed entities and sets enforcement dates. The order authorizes the Treasury, in consultation with State and Defense, to issue rules, report to Congress, and determine removal of prohibitions. All federal agencies must take measures to implement the prohibitions.

title: Blocking Property and Suspending Entry Into the United States of Certain Persons Contributing to the Destabilizing Situation in the Western Balkans
summary: Executive Order 14033 expands an existing national emergency, blocks property of designated persons, suspends their entry into the United States, and delegates authority to the Treasury to implement the measures.

title: Protecting Americans' Sensitive Data From Foreign Adversaries
summary: Executive Order 14034 directs agencies to rescind prior orders, requires multiple reports on data‑security risks, and gives the Secretary of Commerce authority to evaluate connected‑software transactions.
instrument_other_reason: The order performs several distinct actions (delegating authority, directing reports, and rescinding prior orders); each is captured in separate claim objects below.

title: Diversity, Equity, Inclusion, and Accessibility in the Federal Workforce
summary: Executive Order 14035 (June 25 2021) directs the federal government to expand and coordinate a Government‑wide Diversity, Equity, Inclusion, and Accessibility (DEIA) initiative, requires agencies to develop and report on DEIA plans, and delegates authority to the Director of OPM.

title: Promoting Competition in the American Economy
summary: Executive Order 14036 creates a White House Competition Council and directs federal agencies to coordinate, investigate, and take specific actions to promote competition across many sectors of the American economy, including agriculture, health care, finance, transportation, and technology, with numerous reporting and rulemaking deadlines.

title: Strengthening American Leadership in Clean Cars and Trucks
summary: Executive Order 14037 directs federal agencies to consider new vehicle emissions and fuel‑economy rulemakings, sets a 50 % zero‑emission vehicle sales goal for 2030, and establishes coordination and deadline requirements.
instrument_other_reason: sets a policy goal for vehicle sales

title: Blocking Property of Additional Persons Contributing to the Situation in Belarus
summary: Executive Order 14038 expands the national emergency on Belarus, blocks property of designated persons, suspends entry of certain non‑citizens, and delegates authority to the Treasury to implement the sanctions.

title: Blocking Property With Respect to Certain Russian Energy Export Pipelines
summary: Executive Order 14039 blocks property of foreign persons linked to Russian energy export pipelines, exempts waived persons, directs visa and admission implementation, prohibits contributions, evasion transactions, conspiracies, and certain donations, authorizes Treasury rule‑making, and preserves official government and UN transactions.

title: Declassification Reviews of Certain Documents Concerning the Terrorist Attacks of September 11, 2001
summary: Executive Order 14040 directs the Attorney General and agency heads to conduct declassification reviews of 9/11‑related records, sets standards for those reviews, and requires reporting and public release. It references several prior documents and Executive Order 13526.

title: White House Initiative on Advancing Educational Equity, Excellence, and Economic Opportunity Through Historically Black Colleges and Universities
summary: Executive Order 14041 establishes a White House Initiative and a President’s Board of Advisors focused on historically Black colleges and universities (HBCUs). It creates new bodies, requires agencies to submit annual plans, and sets a reporting deadline.

title: Ensuring Adequate COVID Safety Protocols for Federal Contractors
summary: The order delegates authority to the Safer Federal Workforce Task Force, the Federal Acquisition Regulatory Council, and executive agencies to develop and require COVID‑19 safety clauses in federal contracts, with specific deadlines for guidance (Sept 24 2021), FAR amendment (Oct 8 2021), agency implementation (Oct 8 2021), and contract applicability (Oct 15 2021).

title: Requiring Coronavirus Disease 2019 Vaccination for Federal Employees
summary: Executive Order 14043 directs every federal agency to require COVID‑19 vaccination for its employees (with legal exceptions) and tasks the Safer Federal Workforce Task Force with issuing implementation guidance within seven days.

title: Amending Executive Order 14007
summary: Amends Executive Order 14007 to set a maximum of 32 members for the President’s Council of Advisors on Science and Technology (PCAST).

title: White House Initiative on Advancing Educational Equity, Excellence, and Economic Opportunity for Hispanics
summary: Executive Order 14045 creates a White House Initiative, an Interagency Working Group, and a Presidential Advisory Commission to advance educational equity and economic opportunity for Hispanic students and communities.

title: Imposing Sanctions on Certain Persons With Respect to the Humanitarian and Human Rights Crisis in Ethiopia
summary: Executive Order 14046 authorizes the Treasury Secretary to impose sanctions—including blocking property, prohibiting investments, loans, and transactions—on foreign persons linked to the humanitarian and human‑rights crisis in Ethiopia.

title: Adding Measles to the List of Quarantinable Communicable Diseases
summary: Adds measles to the list of quarantinable communicable diseases by amending Executive Order 13295.

title: Continuance or Reestablishment of Certain Federal Advisory Committees and Amendments to Other Executive Orders
summary: Executive Order 14048 continues or re‑establishs a large set of federal advisory committees, assigns their Federal Advisory Committee Act functions to the heads of the designated agencies, supersedes sections of EO 13889, and sets its own effective date.

title: White House Initiative on Advancing Educational Equity, Excellence, and Economic Opportunity for Native Americans and Strengthening Tribal Colleges and Universities
summary: Executive Order 14049 establishes the White House Initiative on Advancing Educational Equity, Excellence, and Economic Opportunity for Native Americans and Strengthening Tribal Colleges and Universities, designates co‑chairs, creates an Executive Director, directs agency plans, requires MOAs within 180 days, and mandates annual reporting to the President.

title: White House Initiative on Advancing Educational Equity, Excellence, and Economic Opportunity for Black Americans
summary: Executive Order 14050 establishes the White House Initiative on Advancing Educational Equity, Excellence, and Economic Opportunity for Black Americans, creates an Interagency Working Group, and forms a Presidential Advisory Commission. It tasks the Secretary of Education to chair the Initiative, directs federal agencies to develop and report Agency Plans, and requires annual reporting to the President. The order also sets a two‑year termination deadline for the Commission.

title: Designation To Exercise Authority Over the National Defense Stockpile
summary: Executive Order 14051 designates the Under Secretary of Defense for Acquisition and Sustainment to release strategic and critical materials from the National Defense Stockpile, limits releases to national‑defense purposes, requires agency consultation before release, and preserves the effect of prior orders and authorities.

title: Implementation of the Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act
summary: The order creates the Infrastructure Implementation Task Force to coordinate implementation of the Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act.

title: Improving Public Safety and Criminal Justice for Native Americans and Addressing the Crisis of Missing or Murdered Indigenous People
summary: Executive Order 14053 directs federal officials to develop strategies, guidance, and plans to improve public safety and criminal justice for Native Americans, and requires multiple reports to the President within specified time‑frames.

title: Termination of Emergency With Respect to the Situation in Burundi
summary: Executive Order 14054 terminates the national emergency concerning Burundi that was declared in Executive Order 13712 and revokes that earlier order. It ends the suspension of entry for immigrants and nonimmigrants who met the criteria of the revoked order, and clarifies that the termination does not affect any prior actions or proceedings. The order also states that it does not impair any existing authority of executive departments or the OMB.

title: Nondisplacement of Qualified Workers Under Service Contracts
summary: Executive Order 14055 establishes a nondisplacement requirement for service‑contract workers and directs agencies, the Secretary of Labor, the FAR Council and OMB to implement it.

title: The National Space Council
summary: Executive Order 14056 establishes the National Space Council’s membership, duties, and a Users’ Advisory Group, and revokes the two prior orders that revived the Council.

title: Catalyzing Clean Energy Industries and Jobs Through Federal Sustainability
summary: Executive Order 14057 establishes new federal bodies to advance clean‑energy and sustainability goals.

title: Transforming Federal Customer Experience and Service Delivery To Rebuild Trust in Government
summary: Executive Order 14058 directs multiple federal secretaries and agency heads to improve customer experience and service delivery, establishes a designation for High‑Impact Service Providers (HISPs), and sets several reporting and planning deadlines.

title: Imposing Sanctions on Foreign Persons Involved in the Global Illicit Drug Trade
summary: Executive Order 14059 imposes sanctions on foreign persons involved in the global illicit drug trade.

title: Establishing the United States Council on Transnational Organized Crime
summary: Executive Order 14060 establishes the United States Council on Transnational Organized Crime (USCTOC), revokes a provision of a prior order, replaces an earlier working group, and sets reporting deadlines.

title: Adjustments of Certain Rates of Pay
summary: The order updates the pay rates and salaries for multiple federal pay systems by publishing new schedules.

title: 2022 Amendments to the Manual for Courts-Martial, United States
summary: Executive Order 14062 amends Parts II and IV of the Manual for Courts‑Martial, United States, and sets the amendments to take effect on the order’s date.

title: Use of Project Labor Agreements for Federal Construction Projects
summary: Executive Order 14063 directs federal agencies to require project‑labor agreements for large‑scale construction projects, gives senior officials authority to grant exceptions, and sets reporting and regulatory‑implementation deadlines. It also revokes Executive Order 13502.

title: Protecting Certain Property of Da Afghanistan Bank for the Benefit of the People of Afghanistan
summary: All property and interests in property of DAB that are held, as of the date of this order, in the United States by any United States financial institution, are blocked

title: Blocking Property of Certain Persons and Prohibiting Certain Transactions With Respect to Continued Russian Efforts To Undermine the Sovereignty and Territorial Integrity of Ukraine
summary: Executive Order 14065 expands the national emergency on Russia’s actions in Ukraine and imposes sanctions – blocking property and prohibiting transactions – while also suspending entry of certain non‑citizens and authorising Treasury to issue implementing rules.

title: Prohibiting Certain Imports and New Investments With Respect to Continued Russian Federation Efforts To Undermine the Sovereignty and Territorial Integrity of Ukraine
summary: Executive Order 14066 expands the national emergency on Russia and imposes trade and investment sanctions against the Russian Federation.

title: Ensuring Responsible Development of Digital Assets
summary: Executive Order 14067 directs inter‑agency coordination, requires multiple reports and assessments, and establishes several deadlines related to digital‑asset policy.  It also references other policy documents.

title: Prohibiting Certain Imports, Exports, and New Investment With Respect to Continued Russian Federation Aggression
summary: Executive Order 14068 imposes sanctions on imports, exports, investment and financial transactions related to the Russian Federation and delegates authority to Treasury and Commerce to implement the order.

title: Advancing Economy, Efficiency, and Effectiveness in Federal Contracting by Promoting Pay Equity and Transparency
summary: Executive Order 14069 directs the Federal Acquisition Regulatory Council, in consultation with the Secretary of Labor and other agency heads, to consider issuing proposed rules that promote economy, efficiency, and effectiveness in federal procurement by enhancing pay equity and transparency for contractors and subcontractors. The order also tasks the council with evaluating whether such rules should limit or prohibit the use of salary history and to include accountability measures. It reaffirms the administration’s policy to eliminate discriminatory pay practices in the federal workforce and procurement.

title: Continuing To Strengthen Americans' Access to Affordable, Quality Health Coverage
summary: Executive Order 14070 directs federal agencies with responsibilities for Medicaid and the Affordable Care Act to review their existing actions and identify ways to expand affordable health coverage.

title: Prohibiting New Investment in and Certain Services to the Russian Federation in Response to Continued Russian Federation Aggression
summary: Executive Order 14071 imposes sanctions on the Russian Federation by prohibiting new investment, certain services, financing, and related activities, while providing exemptions, definitions, and implementation authority.

title: Strengthening the Nation's Forests, Communities, and Local Economies
summary: Executive Order 14072 directs multiple federal secretaries and agencies to inventory old‑growth forests, set reforestation goals, and submit several reports on forest conservation, international deforestation, and nature‑based solutions, with key deadlines of one year for inventories and reports and a 2030 target for reforestation.

title: Enhancing the National Quantum Initiative Advisory Committee
summary: Executive Order 14073 establishes the National Quantum Initiative Advisory Committee to advise the President and NSTC subcommittees on quantum information science and its technology applications. It defines the Committee’s composition, duties, and meeting requirements, and directs federal agencies to provide information, technical support, and security clearances as needed. The order revokes the earlier EO 13885 that created a prior committee and cites statutory authority under the National Quantum Initiative Act and Title 3 of the U.S. Code.

title: Advancing Effective, Accountable Policing and Criminal Justice Practices To Enhance Public Trust and Public Safety
summary: Executive Order 14074 creates new interagency bodies (a recruitment‑focused working group and a Federal Interagency Alternatives and Reentry Committee), establishes a National Law Enforcement Accountability Database, and issues a series of timed directives—reports, studies, policy‑issuance and grant‑review actions—across law‑enforcement, health, and technology domains, while superseding any conflicting prior orders.

title: Advancing Equality for Lesbian, Gay, Bisexual, Transgender, Queer, and Intersex Individuals
summary: Executive Order 14075 creates several new inter‑agency bodies and directs multiple agencies to develop policies, studies, guidance, and reports with specific deadlines.

title: Protecting Access to Reproductive Healthcare Services
summary: Executive Order 14076 establishes an interagency task force on reproductive‑healthcare access, directs a 30‑day report to the President, and assigns various agencies duties to protect access, privacy, and safety.

title: Establishing an Emergency Board To Investigate Disputes Between Certain Railroads Represented by the National Carriers' Conference Committee of the National Railway Labor Conference and Their Employees Represented by Certain Labor Organizations
summary: Executive Order 14077 creates an Emergency Board to investigate specific railroad‑labor disputes and directs it to report within 30 days.

title: Bolstering Efforts To Bring Hostages and Wrongfully Detained United States Nationals Home
summary: Executive Order 14078 establishes new coordination and reporting duties, continues prior hostage‑recovery directives, and imposes sanctions on persons linked to hostage‑taking or wrongful detention.
instrument_other_reason: The order’s main actions are a mix of delegating authority, directing reports and imposing sanctions; no single listed instrument dominates.

title: Securing Access to Reproductive and Other Healthcare Services
summary: Executive Order 14079 directs the Secretary of Health and Human Services to take actions that improve access to reproductive and other healthcare services. It tasks HHS with considering measures to expand Medicaid coverage across state lines, ensuring compliance with federal non‑discrimination laws, and evaluating data collection on maternal health outcomes. The order does not create a new entity but delegates authority to HHS to develop guidance, technical assistance, and other actions to protect reproductive health access.

title: Implementation of the CHIPS Act of 2022
summary: Executive Order 14080 establishes the CHIPS Implementation Steering Council to coordinate the implementation of the CHIPS Act across the executive branch. It directs all federal agencies to prioritize protecting taxpayer resources, building domestic semiconductor capacity, and fostering private‑sector investment. The order also tasks the Director of the Office of Management and Budget with overseeing stewardship of taxpayer funds and sets the Co‑Chairs of the Council.

title: Advancing Biotechnology and Biomanufacturing Innovation for a Sustainable, Safe, and Secure American Bioeconomy
summary: Executive Order 14081 establishes several new bodies (Data for the Bioeconomy Initiative, Biosafety and Biosecurity Innovation Initiative, Interagency Technical Working Group) and directs a wide‑ranging set of reports, plans, and assessments across agencies, each with specific deadlines ranging from 90 days to 2 years, to advance biotechnology and biomanufacturing for health, climate, security, and economic goals.

title: Implementation of the Energy and Infrastructure Provisions of the Inflation Reduction Act of 2022
summary: Executive Order 14082 establishes new offices and working groups, amends prior orders, and directs agency priorities to implement the Inflation Reduction Act’s energy and infrastructure provisions.
instrument_other_reason: The order contains multiple distinct actions; each is captured as a separate claim below.

title: Ensuring Robust Consideration of Evolving National Security Risks by the Committee on Foreign Investment in the United States
summary: Executive Order 14083 directs the Committee on Foreign Investment in the United States (CFIUS) to expand its review factors, assigns the Office of Science and Technology Policy (OSTP) the task of publishing sector lists, and requires CFIUS to periodically report on its review process.

title: Promoting the Arts, the Humanities, and Museum and Library Services
summary: Executive Order 14084 establishes a new advisory body, the President’s Committee on the Arts and the Humanities, within the Institute of Museum and Library Services (IMLS). The order also sets the committee’s composition, advisory role, meeting frequency, and a two‑year termination deadline, and it references Executive Order 13985.
topic_other_reason: The order’s subject is the promotion of the arts, humanities, museum and library services – a cultural‑policy area not covered by the listed topics.

title: Expanding Eligibility for Certain Military Decorations and Awards
summary: Executive Order 14085 expands eligibility for certain military decorations and awards by amending several prior executive orders that govern those awards.
topic_other_reason: The order’s subject is the eligibility criteria for military decorations and awards, which falls under the administration of federal award programs.

title: Enhancing Safeguards for United States Signals Intelligence Activities
summary: Executive Order 14086 creates new oversight bodies, assigns officials new duties, and sets several time‑bound actions to strengthen privacy and civil‑liberties safeguards for U.S. signals‑intelligence activities.
instrument_other_reason: The order primarily establishes policy safeguards rather than a listed instrument.

title: Lowering Prescription Drug Costs for Americans
summary: The order directs the Secretary of Health and Human Services to submit a report within 90 days describing any health‑care payment and delivery models selected for testing to lower prescription‑drug costs.

title: Taking Additional Steps To Address the National Emergency With Respect to the Situation in Nicaragua
summary: Executive Order 14088 amends Executive Order 13851 to add and replace subsections that expand sanctions‑related prohibitions and authorizations concerning Nicaragua.

title: Establishing the President's Advisory Council on African Diaspora Engagement in the United States
summary: Executive Order 14089 establishes the President’s Advisory Council on African Diaspora Engagement within the Department of State.

title: Adjustments of Certain Rates of Pay
summary: Executive Order 14090 adjusts the rates of basic pay for various federal pay systems, sets effective dates for the new schedules, and directs the Director of the Office of Personnel Management to implement locality‑based comparability payments.

title: Further Advancing Racial Equity and Support for Underserved Communities Through the Federal Government
summary: Executive Order 14091 expands the federal government’s equity agenda by creating agency‑level Equity Teams and a White House Steering Committee on Equity, reinstating two earlier orders, and setting a series of reporting and planning deadlines.

title: Reducing Gun Violence and Making Our Communities Safer
summary: Executive Order 14092 directs multiple federal officials to take actions and submit reports aimed at reducing gun violence.

title: Prohibition on Use by the United States Government of Commercial Spyware That Poses Risks to National Security
summary: Executive Order 14093 prohibits U.S. government operational use of commercial spyware and assigns a series of inter‑agency duties, reporting, and assessment requirements.

title: Modernizing Regulatory Review
summary: Executive Order 14094 amends the definition of “significant regulatory action” in EO 12866, directs agencies to keep a log of rule‑making petitions, and orders the OMB Director to revise Circular A‑4 within one year.

title: Increasing Access to High-Quality Care and Supporting Caregivers
summary: Executive Order 14095 directs multiple federal secretaries and agencies to issue guidance, consider rulemaking, conduct studies, and launch pilot programs aimed at improving the child‑care, long‑term‑care and caregiver workforce.

title: Revitalizing Our Nation's Commitment to Environmental Justice for All
summary: Executive Order 14096 establishes a White House Office of Environmental Justice and related bodies, directing agencies to develop strategic plans, assessments, and reporting on environmental‑justice issues.

title: Authority To Order the Ready Reserve of the Armed Forces to Active Duty To Address International Drug Trafficking
summary: Executive Order 14097 invokes emergency authority under the National Emergencies Act and 10 U.S.C. §12302 to allow the Secretary of Defense and the Secretary of Homeland Security, as well as the Secretaries of the Army, Navy, Air Force, and the Coast Guard, to order units and individual members of the Ready Reserve to active duty in order to address the national emergency posed by international drug trafficking. The order reaffirms that it does not impair existing statutory authority or create enforceable rights, and it is subject to the availability of appropriations.

title: Imposing Sanctions on Certain Persons Destabilizing Sudan and Undermining the Goal of a Democratic Transition
summary: Executive Order 14098 expands the national‑emergency sanctions regime against persons destabilizing Sudan, blocks their property, suspends their entry to the United States, and delegates implementation authority to senior officials.  It also references and continues earlier Sudan‑related orders.

title: Moving Beyond COVID-19 Vaccination Requirements for Federal Workers
summary: The order revokes the earlier vaccination‑requirement orders for federal employees and contractors.

title: Advancing Economic Security for Military and Veteran Spouses, Military Caregivers, and Survivors
summary: Executive Order 14100 directs multiple federal agencies—primarily OPM, DoD, State, Labor, Veterans Affairs, Homeland Security, OSTP, and SBA—to develop a Government‑wide strategic plan and related actions that improve hiring, retention, training, telework, child‑care support, and entrepreneurial resources for military‑connected spouses, caregivers, and survivors. The order requires the plan within 180 days, updates reporting titles by FY 2025, mandates flexible spending accounts by 1 Jan 2024, and calls for inter‑agency coordination, data‑tracking recommendations, and new guidance on telework and administrative leave.

title: Strengthening Access to Affordable, High-Quality Contraception and Family Planning Services
summary: Executive Order 14101 directs multiple federal secretaries to consider actions that improve access to affordable, high‑quality contraception and family‑planning services.

title: Ordering the Selected Reserve and Certain Members of the Individual Ready Reserve of the Armed Forces to Active Duty
summary: Executive Order 14102 authorizes the Secretaries of Defense and Homeland Security (for the Coast Guard) to order selected reserve and certain Individual Ready Reserve members to active duty, limited to 3,000 total members (no more than 450 from the IRR).

title: 2023 Amendments to the Manual for Courts-Martial, United States
summary: Executive Order 14103 amends the Manual for Courts‑Martial (the UCMJ manual) by adding new appendices and revising several parts, with some changes taking effect immediately and others tied to dates set by the 2022 National‑Defense Authorization Act.

title: Federal Research and Development in Support of Domestic Manufacturing and United States Jobs
summary: Executive Order 14104 directs federal agencies to prioritize domestic manufacturing in federally‑funded research and development, to require reporting on the location of inventions, and to establish processes for waivers and reporting. The order delegates authority to agency heads and sets multiple reporting deadlines.

title: Addressing United States Investments in Certain National Security Technologies and Products in Countries of Concern
summary: Executive Order 14105 declares a national emergency concerning United States investments that could aid countries of concern in developing sensitive national‑security technologies. It directs the Secretary of the Treasury, in consultation with other agencies, to issue regulations that require notification of certain transactions and prohibit others, and tasks the Secretary with reporting to the President and Congress and reviewing the regulations annually.

title: United States Coast Guard Officer Personnel Management
summary: Executive Order 14106 delegates a range of personnel‑management authorities for the United States Coast Guard from the President to the Secretary of Homeland Security, and further extends those delegated powers during war or national emergency.
topic_other_reason: The order deals specifically with the internal personnel management of a uniformed service, which is a function of the executive branch rather than a broader defense policy area.

title: Exemption of Paul H. Maurer From Mandatory Separation
summary: Executive Order 14107 exempts Special Agent Paul H. Maurer, the Special Agent in Charge of the George W. Bush Protective Detail, from the automatic separation provision of 5 U.S.C. §8425(b)(1). The President determines that the public interest requires the exemption and directs that the Director of the United States Secret Service retain all supervisory authority over Maurer. The order includes standard general provisions stating it does not create any enforceable right and is subject to applicable law and appropriations.
instrument_other_reason: exempts a specific employee from mandatory separation under 5 U.S.C. §8425(b)(1)

title: Ensuring the People of East Palestine Are Protected Now and in the Future
summary: Executive Order 14108 directs federal agencies to support long‑term recovery, environmental cleanup, public‑health monitoring and transportation safety after the East Palestine train derailment.

title: Continuance of Certain Federal Advisory Committees and Amendments to Other Executive Orders
summary: Executive Order 14109 continues a list of federal advisory committees through 30 Sept 2025 and supersedes sections 1‑2 of EO 14048.
instrument_other_reason: the order extends the existence of existing advisory committees (no listed instrument matches)

title: Safe, Secure, and Trustworthy Development and Use of Artificial Intelligence
summary: Executive Order 14110 establishes a White House Artificial Intelligence Council and directs a series of agency‑wide actions to govern the development and use of AI.

title: Interagency Security Committee
summary: Executive Order 14111 establishes the Interagency Security Committee to improve security and protection of Federal facilities.

title: Reforming Federal Funding and Support for Tribal Nations To Better Embrace Our Trust Responsibilities and Promote the Next Era of Tribal Self-Determination
summary: EO 14112 delegates authority to the OMB Director and Domestic Policy Advisor to lead a review of Tribal Nations funding, requires agency heads to report funding needs within 540 days, and mandates guidance development within 240 days.

title: Adjustments of Certain Rates of Pay

title: Establishment of the Strategic Bitcoin Reserve and United States Digital Asset Stockpile
summary: Executive Order 14233 creates two new Treasury offices to hold and manage government‑owned cryptocurrency and other digital assets, and it imposes a series of reporting and evaluation deadlines for agencies and the Treasury.

title: Establishing the White House Task Force on the FIFA World Cup 2026
summary: Executive Order 14234 establishes a White House Task Force to coordinate the 2025 FIFA Club World Cup and the 2026 FIFA World Cup, directs agencies to submit reports, and sets a termination date for the Task Force.

title: Restoring Public Service Loan Forgiveness
summary: Executive Order 14235 directs the Secretary of Education to revise the Public Service Loan Forgiveness regulations to exclude organizations with substantial illegal purposes and declares that employees of such organizations are ineligible for loan forgiveness.

title: Additional Rescissions of Harmful Executive Orders and Actions
summary: Executive Order 14236 rescinds a series of prior executive actions.

title: Addressing Risks From Paul Weiss
summary: Executive Order 14237 directs federal agencies to suspend security clearances for individuals associated with the law firm Paul Weiss, halt provision of government goods and services to the firm, and require contractors to disclose any business with Paul Weiss. It mandates agency heads to review and, where permissible, terminate contracts with the firm and submit a compliance assessment to the Office of Management and Budget within 30 days. The order also limits access to federal facilities and employment of Paul Weiss personnel, citing national security and anti‑discrimination concerns.

title: Continuing the Reduction of the Federal Bureaucracy
summary: Executive Order 14238 directs the elimination of non‑statutory components of seven federal entities, requires heads of those entities to submit compliance reports to OMB within 7 days (by 2025‑03‑21), and instructs OMB to reject any funding requests inconsistent with the order.

title: Achieving Efficiency Through State and Local Preparedness
summary: The order directs the Assistant to the President for National Security Affairs and other officials to review and update a series of federal policies and to create a National Resilience Strategy, a National Risk Register, and other deliverables, thereby delegating authority to senior officials to carry out these tasks.
topic_other_reason: The order is focused on the overall coordination of federal preparedness and resilience policy rather than a specific sector such as energy, justice, or technology.

title: Eliminating Waste and Saving Taxpayer Dollars by Consolidating Procurement
summary: Executive Order 14240 directs the consolidation of domestic federal procurement in the General Services Administration and assigns new procurement‑related authority to the GSA Administrator.

title: Immediate Measures To Increase American Mineral Production
summary: Executive Order 14241 directs federal agencies to accelerate domestic mineral production by delegating Defense‑Production‑Act authority, setting rapid reporting and permitting timelines, and coordinating land‑use, financing and regulatory actions.

title: Improving Education Outcomes by Empowering Parents, States, and Communities
summary: Executive Order 14242 directs the Secretary of Education to close the Department of Education and return education authority to the states and local communities. It also requires the Secretary to ensure federal education funds are allocated in compliance with law and to eliminate programs that discriminate under the guise of diversity, equity, and inclusion. The order emphasizes uninterrupted delivery of services while the department is being shut down.

title: Stopping Waste, Fraud, and Abuse by Eliminating Information Silos
summary: The order directs agency heads to grant prompt access to unclassified data, remove barriers, report on regulations and classified‑information policies, give the Labor Secretary access to unemployment data, and supersede earlier orders that impede data sharing.

title: Addressing Remedial Action by Paul Weiss
summary: Executive Order 14244 revokes the earlier Executive Order 14237.

title: Imposing Tariffs on Countries Importing Venezuelan Oil
summary: The order imposes a 25 percent tariff on goods from any country that imports Venezuelan oil and directs the Secretary of State (with other secretaries) to determine and enforce the tariff.

title: Addressing Risks From Jenner & Block
summary: Executive Order 14246 directs federal agencies to suspend security clearances, cease provision of government goods and services, require contractor disclosures, review and potentially terminate contracts, and limit access and hiring of Jenner & Block personnel; agencies must submit a contract‑assessment report within 30 days.

title: Modernizing Payments To and From America's Bank Account
summary: Executive Order 14247 directs the federal government to replace paper‑based payments with electronic methods, establishes limited exceptions, requires public outreach, and sets reporting deadlines.

title: Preserving and Protecting the Integrity of American Elections
summary: Executive Order 14248 (2025‑03‑25) directs multiple federal agencies to tighten citizenship verification for voter registration, improve voting‑system security, and enforce existing election‑law statutes. It delegates new duties to the Election Assistance Commission, the Department of Homeland Security, the Attorney General, and other officials, and it orders the cessation of actions taken under EO 14019.

title: Protecting America's Bank Account Against Fraud, Waste, and Abuse
summary: Executive Order 14249 directs the Treasury and other federal officials to improve payment verification, consolidate financial systems, reduce non‑Treasury disbursing offices, and require agencies to submit compliance plans and reports, with multiple statutory deadlines ranging from 30 to 180 days.
topic_other_reason: The order’s focus is on improving financial management and payment integrity across the federal government.
instrument_other_reason: The order primarily directs agencies and officials to issue guidance, modify records notices, and assess delegations, actions not captured by the listed instrument categories.

title: Addressing Risks From WilmerHale
summary: Executive Order 14250 directs federal agencies to treat the law firm Wilmer Hale as a national‑security risk, suspending its personnel’s clearances, halting government support, demanding contract disclosures, allowing contract terminations, and requiring agencies to report on related contracts within 30 days. It also affirms that the order does not limit actions in EO 14230 and ties agency funding decisions to EO 14147.

title: Exclusions From Federal Labor-Management Relations Programs
summary: Executive Order 14251 modifies the federal labor‑management relations framework for national‑security‑related agencies, amends EO 12171, delegates exclusion authority to several secretaries, and imposes reporting and certification deadlines.

title: Making the District of Columbia Safe and Beautiful
summary: Executive Order 14252 creates a D.C. Safe and Beautiful Task Force, directs the Secretary of the Interior to order the National Park Service to clean up encampments and graffiti, and requires the Task Force to report to the President.

title: Restoring Truth and Sanity to American History
summary: Executive Order 14253 directs the Vice President, the Office of Management and Budget, and the Secretary of the Interior to restore historically accurate narratives at federal museums, monuments, and historic sites. It mandates the removal of ideological content from Smithsonian exhibits, requires funding to improve Independence National Historical Park by July 4 2026, and orders the Interior Department to assess and, if necessary, reinstate public monuments altered since 2020. The order also directs the Vice President to seek appointment of citizen members to the Smithsonian Board of Regents and delegates authority to agencies to implement these policies.

title: Combating Unfair Practices in the Live Entertainment Market
summary: Executive Order 14254 directs federal agencies to enforce competition and consumer‑protection laws in the live‑entertainment ticket market and requires a joint report within 180 days.

title: Establishing the United States Investment Accelerator
summary: Executive Order 14255 creates a new office – the United States Investment Accelerator – within the Department of Commerce to accelerate large‑scale investments, designates its leadership, and assigns it responsibility for the existing CHIPS Program Office.

title: Further Amendment to Duties Addressing the Synthetic Opioid Supply Chain in the People's Republic of China as Applied to Low-Value Imports
summary: The order removes the de‑minimis exemption for low‑value imports from the People’s Republic of China (including Hong Kong) and imposes new ad‑valorem and specific duties on those shipments, authorizing Customs and Border Protection (CBP) to collect and remit the duties, require carrier bonds, and direct the U.S. International Trade Commission to update the Harmonized Tariff Schedule.

title: Regulating Imports With a Reciprocal Tariff To Rectify Trade Practices That Contribute to Large and Persistent Annual United States Goods Trade Deficits
summary: Executive Order 14257 imposes a 10 percent ad‑valorem tariff on all imports and higher, country‑specific rates for listed partners, effective 5 April 2025 (general) and 9 April 2025 (specific). It modifies the HTSUS, continues a prior opioid‑related order, and terminates or suspends any earlier directives that conflict with its provisions.

title: Extending the TikTok Enforcement Delay
summary: The order extends the TikTok enforcement delay, amending EO 14166, with deadline June 19, 2025.

title: Amendment to Reciprocal Tariffs and Updated Duties as Applied to Low-Value Imports From the People's Republic of China
summary: Executive Order 14259 raises U.S. tariff rates on selected Chinese goods and increases de‑minimis duties, effective in April‑June 2025.

title: Protecting American Energy From State Overreach
summary: Executive Order 14260 directs the Attorney General to identify and halt enforcement of state laws that impede domestic energy resources and requires a report within 60 days.

title: Reinvigorating America's Beautiful Clean Coal Industry and Amending Executive Order 14241
summary: Executive Order 14261 (April 8 2025) amends Executive Order 14241 to treat coal as a mineral, directs multiple agencies to assess and remove barriers to coal production, and sets a series of reporting and review deadlines.

title: Strengthening the Reliability and Security of the United States Electric Grid
summary: The order directs the Secretary of Energy to streamline and expedite DOE processes for issuing orders under the Federal Power Act, and to develop and publish a uniform methodology for assessing reserve margins across the bulk‑power system. It requires the methodology to be created within 30 days and posted online within 90 days, and establishes a protocol for identifying critical generation resources. The order is issued under presidential constitutional authority and references the national energy emergency declared in EO 14156.

title: Addressing Risks From Susman Godfrey
summary: Executive Order 14263 directs federal agencies to restrict security clearances, contracts, hiring, and access for the law firm Susman Godfrey and to report on related contracts within 30 days.

title: Maintaining Acceptable Water Pressure in Showerheads
summary: Executive Order 14264 directs the Secretary of Energy to rescind a prior Energy Conservation Program regulation defining “showerhead,” making the repeal effective 30 days after the notice is published.

title: Modernizing Defense Acquisitions and Spurring Innovation in the Defense Industrial Base
summary: Executive Order 14265 creates a new formal steering board (the Configuration Steering Board) to manage acquisition‑program risk and directs multiple deadline‑driven plans and reviews for defense acquisition reform.

title: Modifying Reciprocal Tariff Rates To Reflect Trading Partner Retaliation and Alignment
summary: Executive Order 14266 modifies the Harmonized Tariff Schedule to impose additional ad valorem duties on imports from the People's Republic of China and other foreign trading partners in response to retaliatory measures. It suspends certain country‑specific tariff rates for a 90‑day period and raises duties on selected headings, while also increasing de minimis tariff rates and postal item duties. The order directs the Secretaries of Commerce, Homeland Security, the U.S. Trade Representative and other senior officials to implement the changes through regulations and other actions.

title: Reducing Anti-Competitive Regulatory Barriers
summary: This order directs the heads of federal agencies to review all regulations under their rulemaking authority and identify those that create anti‑competitive effects. It requires agency heads to submit lists of such regulations within 70 days, the FTC Chairman to issue a public request for information within 10 days, and the Chairman to deliver a consolidated list to the OMB Director within 90 days of receiving agency submissions. The OMB Director, together with the Office of Information and Regulatory Affairs, will decide whether to incorporate rescissions or modifications into the Unified Regulatory Agenda.

title: Reforming Foreign Defense Sales To Improve Speed and Accountability
summary: Executive Order 14268 directs the Secretaries of State and Defense (and, where noted, the Secretary of Commerce) to take a series of actions to reform the foreign defense sales system, including developing priority‑partner lists, updating the FMS‑Only List, and submitting plans and reports within specified time‑frames.  It also implements National Security Presidential Memorandum 10 (2018) and requires annual review of certain lists.

title: Restoring America's Maritime Dominance
summary: Executive Order 14269 directs multiple agencies to develop a Maritime Action Plan (MAP) and related reports, incentives, and reviews to restore U.S. maritime industrial capacity and security.

title: Zero-Based Regulatory Budgeting To Unleash American Energy
summary: Executive Order 14270 directs a set of federal agencies that regulate energy‑related activities to adopt zero‑based regulatory budgeting by issuing sunset rules that place a Conditional Sunset Date on existing and new regulations, with the first sunset rules to be effective no later than 30 September 2025 and a required list of applicable statutes to be submitted by EPA and the Army Corps of Engineers within 30 days of the order.

title: Ensuring Commercial, Cost-Effective Solutions in Federal Contracts
summary: Executive Order 14271 directs federal agencies to prioritize commercially available products in procurement and sets review, assessment, and reporting requirements.

title: Ensuring National Security and Economic Resilience Through Section 232 Actions on Processed Critical Minerals and Derivative Products
summary: Executive Order 14272 directs the Secretary of Commerce to conduct a Section 232 investigation of imports of processed critical minerals and their derivative products, and to produce interim and final reports on the findings.

title: Lowering Drug Prices by Once Again Putting Americans First
summary: Executive Order 14273 directs multiple federal officials to take actions aimed at lowering prescription drug prices for Americans. It tasks the Secretary of Health and Human Services, the Assistant to the President for Domestic and Economic Policy, the OMB Director, the Secretary of Labor, and other officials with developing guidance, reporting, and regulatory proposals related to Medicare, Medicaid, drug importation, and pharmacy benefit manager transparency. The order sets specific deadlines for these actions, ranging from 60 days to one year after the order’s issuance. It references the Inflation Reduction Act but does not revoke or amend any prior executive order.

title: Restoring Common Sense to Federal Office Space Management
summary: Executive Order 14274 revokes two prior orders on federal space management, directs the Administrator of General Services to amend related regulations, and requires agencies using federal space to conform to the new policy.

title: Restoring Common Sense to Federal Procurement
summary: The order directs the Administrator and agency heads to amend the Federal Acquisition Regulation within 180 days, requires each agency to name a senior procurement official within 15 days, mandates the OMB Director to issue implementation guidance within 20 days, and sets sunset provisions for non‑statutory FAR items to expire four years after final rule adoption unless renewed.

title: Restoring American Seafood Competitiveness
summary: Executive Order 14276 directs the Secretary of Commerce and other officials to take a series of actions aimed at improving U.S. seafood competitiveness.

title: Advancing Artificial Intelligence Education for American Youth
summary: Executive Order 14277 creates a White House Task Force on Artificial Intelligence Education and directs a series of actions, reports and deadlines to develop AI‑focused education programs, a national AI challenge, teacher‑training, public‑private partnerships, and apprenticeship initiatives.

title: Preparing Americans for High-Paying Skilled Trade Jobs of the Future
summary: The order directs the Secretaries of Labor, Commerce, and Education to review federal workforce‑development programs and submit a report, and to submit a plan to expand registered apprenticeships, each within specified time limits.

title: Reforming Accreditation To Strengthen Higher Education
summary: Executive Order 14279 directs the Secretary of Education and the Attorney General to hold higher‑education accreditors accountable for unlawful discrimination, to investigate and terminate such practices, and to establish new student‑oriented accreditation principles. It authorizes the Secretary of Education to recognize new accreditors, require data‑driven outcomes, and launch an experimental site under the Higher Education Act. The order also requires consultation with the Secretary of Health and Human Services on medical‑school accreditation issues. It is grounded in presidential constitutional authority and specific statutory provisions.

title: Reinstating Commonsense School Discipline Policies
summary: Executive Order 14280 directs federal officials to issue guidance, take enforcement actions, coordinate with state officials, and submit a report on school‑discipline practices, and it ties its definitions to a prior 2025 order.

title: Restoring Equality of Opportunity and Meritocracy
summary: Executive Order 14281 directs federal agencies to eliminate disparate‑impact liability, revokes two historic presidential approvals of Title VI regulations, and imposes a series of reporting, assessment and guidance duties on the Attorney General and other officials.
instrument_other_reason: The order contains multiple distinct actions; each is recorded as a separate entry below.

title: Transparency Regarding Foreign Influence at American Universities
summary: Executive Order 14282 directs the Secretary of Education to enforce existing foreign‑funding disclosure requirements for higher‑education institutions and to make compliance a condition for receiving federal grants.

title: White House Initiative To Promote Excellence and Innovation at Historically Black Colleges and Universities
summary: Executive Order 14283 establishes a White House Initiative on Historically Black Colleges and Universities and a President’s Board of Advisors on HBCUs, and directs the EPA Administrator to terminate an advisory council within 14 days.

title: Strengthening Probationary Periods in the Federal Service
summary: Executive Order 14284 strengthens probationary and trial periods for Federal employees by superseding subpart H of part 315, title 5, CFR; rescinding that subpart via a new OPM rule within 30 days; amending Civil Service Rule II to delete section 2.4; adding a new Civil Service Rule XI; and directing agencies to identify and evaluate employees in initial probationary or trial periods within 15 days, with certification requirements before finalizing appointments.

title: Unleashing America's Offshore Critical Minerals and Resources
summary: Executive Order 14285 directs multiple federal officials to accelerate offshore seabed‑mineral development, chiefly by delegating authority to expedite permitting and by requiring a series of reports and plans within 60 days.
instrument_other_reason: The order contains several distinct actions (delegating authority, directing reports, and setting deadlines); each claim below is classified individually.

title: Enforcing Commonsense Rules of the Road for America's Truck Drivers
summary: Executive Order 14286 directs the Department of Transportation to rescind an existing guidance on English‑language testing for commercial drivers, issue new guidance, revise out‑of‑service criteria, review non‑domiciled CDLs, improve credential‑verification protocols, and begin actions to improve truck‑driver working conditions.
topic_other_reason: The order’s substantive focus is on transportation safety and driver qualifications, which falls under the Transportation & Infrastructure domain.

title: Protecting American Communities From Criminal Aliens
summary: Executive Order 14287 directs the Attorney General and the Secretary of Homeland Security to publish and update a list of sanctuary jurisdictions within 30 days, notify those jurisdictions, suspend or terminate federal funds to non‑compliant jurisdictions, pursue legal remedies, develop eligibility‑verification guidance for federal benefits, and stop state or local laws that favor aliens over Americans.

title: Strengthening and Unleashing America's Law Enforcement To Pursue Criminals and Protect Innocent Citizens
summary: Executive Order 14288 directs the Attorney General, the Secretary of Defense, the Secretary of Homeland Security and other agency heads to take a series of actions that support state‑ and local‑law‑enforcement.  The order’s primary subject is law‑enforcement policy and its main instrument is the delegation of authority to officials and agencies.

title: Addressing Certain Tariffs on Imported Articles
summary: The order establishes a non‑stacking policy for tariffs listed in section 2, permits additional tariffs between sections 2(d) and 2(e) when conditions are met, preserves the applicability of all other duties and fees, delegates authority to the Secretary of Homeland Security to determine and implement necessary changes to the Harmonized Tariff Schedule of the United States, and sets a May 16, 2025 deadline for those changes.

title: Ending Taxpayer Subsidization of Biased Media
summary: Executive Order 14290 directs the Corporation for Public Broadcasting (CPB) and all federal agencies to end all direct and indirect federal funding for National Public Radio (NPR) and the Public Broadcasting Service (PBS). It also sets a June 30 2025 deadline for the CPB Board to revise grant eligibility rules to prohibit such funding and tasks the Secretary of Health and Human Services with compliance monitoring.
topic_other_reason: The order concerns the federal funding of public‑broadcasting entities, which falls under the administration of government programs rather than a specific sector such as defense or health.
