title: Establishment of the Religious Liberty Commission
summary: Executive Order 14291 establishes the Religious Liberty Commission, defines its composition, term limits, duties, funding, and termination.

title: Improving the Safety and Security of Biological Research
summary: Executive Order 14292 directs the Office of Science and Technology Policy (OSTP) to revise existing federal policies, end funding for certain gain‑of‑function research, and create reporting and enforcement mechanisms for dangerous biological research.

title: Regulatory Relief To Promote Domestic Production of Critical Medicines
summary: Executive Order 14293 directs multiple agencies to streamline regulations and permitting for domestic pharmaceutical manufacturing.

title: Fighting Overcriminalization in Federal Regulations
summary: Executive Order 14294 directs federal agencies to report, assess, and publish information about criminal regulatory offenses and to add transparency requirements to future rulemaking. The order’s primary focus is on criminal‑law enforcement and it principally *directs reports or studies*.

title: Increasing Efficiency at the Office of the Federal Register
summary: Executive Order 14295 directs the Archivist of the United States, acting through the Office of the Federal Register, to improve the speed and cost‑effectiveness of publishing rules and to report on progress.

title: Keeping Promises to Veterans and Establishing a National Center for Warrior Independence
summary: Extracted factual actions, relationships and deadlines from Executive Order 14296 (May 9 2025). Each entry includes a short verbatim quote, the primary policy topic, the instrument type, any relationships the order asserts, and any deadlines it imposes.

title: Delivering Most-Favored-Nation Prescription Drug Pricing to American Patients
summary: Executive Order 14297 directs several senior officials to act on prescription‑drug pricing and sets a 30‑day deadline for the Secretary of Health and Human Services to communicate price targets.

title: Modifying Reciprocal Tariff Rates To Reflect Discussions With the People's Republic of China
summary: Executive Order 14298 modifies the Harmonized Tariff Schedule to suspend, reduce, and re‑set ad valorem duties on imports from the People’s Republic of China for a 90‑day period beginning 14 May 2025, amends several prior tariff‑related orders (EO 14257, EO 14259, EO 14266, EO 14256), and directs multiple cabinet‑level officials to take the actions needed to implement these changes.

title: Deploying Advanced Nuclear Reactor Technologies for National Security
summary: Executive Order 14299 directs the Department of Defense and the Department of Energy to accelerate the development, deployment and export of advanced nuclear reactor technologies for national‑security purposes.  It delegates a range of authorities to senior officials, sets a series of near‑term milestones, and designates the Secretary of the Army as the executive agent for nuclear‑energy programs within the Defense Department.

title: Ordering the Reform of the Nuclear Regulatory Commission
summary: Executive Order 14300 directs the Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) to create a new dedicated team, to issue rulemaking notices and final rules within set time‑frames, and to impose fixed licensing decision deadlines for new and existing reactors.

title: Reforming Nuclear Reactor Testing at the Department of Energy
summary: Executive Order 14301 directs the Department of Energy to accelerate advanced nuclear reactor testing and deployment.
instrument_other_reason: The order contains multiple distinct actions; each is listed separately below.

title: Reinvigorating the Nuclear Industrial Base
summary: Executive Order 14302 directs multiple federal agencies to revitalize the United States nuclear industrial base by requiring a comprehensive report on the nuclear fuel cycle, developing plans to expand uranium conversion and enrichment capacity, halting certain plutonium programs, updating uranium management policy, and seeking voluntary agreements with domestic nuclear companies under the Defense Production Act. It also mandates prioritizing uprates of existing reactors, constructing new advanced reactors, and expanding funding and workforce development for nuclear technologies. The order sets specific deadlines for reports, plans, and agreements, and cites several statutory authorities.

title: Restoring Gold Standard Science
summary: Executive Order 14303 directs the OSTP Director and agency heads to issue guidance, update policies, and report on the implementation of “Gold Standard Science,” and it sets short‑term compliance deadlines while revoking prior organizational changes tied to a 2021 Presidential Memorandum.

title: Leading the World in Supersonic Flight
summary: Executive Order 14304 directs federal agencies to remove regulatory barriers to over‑land supersonic flight, to develop noise‑based certification standards, to coordinate research, and to engage internationally on supersonic aviation.
topic_other_reason: The order’s actions span transportation, technology, and foreign policy, but the dominant focus is on federal regulatory administration of aviation.

title: Restoring American Airspace Sovereignty
summary: Executive Order 14305 (June 6 2025) directs the federal government to protect U.S. airspace from unlawful unmanned‑aircraft‑system (UAS) activity. It creates a new task force, assigns a series of duties to the FAA, the Attorney General, the Department of Homeland Security and other agencies, and sets several time‑bound reporting and rule‑making deadlines.

title: Sustaining Select Efforts To Strengthen the Nation's Cybersecurity and Amending Executive Order 13694 and Executive Order 14144
summary: Executive Order 14306 amends Executive Orders 14144 and 13694 to update U.S. cybersecurity policy. It directs the Secretary of Commerce, through NIST, to create a consortium, update guidance, and publish revisions to the Secure Software Development Framework. The order also tasks the Secretaries of Homeland Security, Defense, Energy, and other officials with actions on post‑quantum cryptography, artificial‑intelligence security, and rules‑as‑code pilots, setting multiple deadlines through 2030.

title: Unleashing American Drone Dominance
summary: Executive Order 14307 directs multiple federal agencies to accelerate the development, commercialization, and export of unmanned aircraft systems (UAS) and eVTOL technologies. It sets a series of near‑term deadlines for rulemaking, reporting, and pilot program actions, and it requires agencies to prioritize U.S.-made drone components and to secure the drone supply chain. The order also amends export controls and establishes reporting requirements for the Department of Defense and the Department of Commerce.

title: Empowering Commonsense Wildfire Prevention and Response
summary: Extracted actionable provisions from Executive Order 14308 (June 12 2025). Each entry records the claim, a short source quote, primary topic, instrument, any relationships, and the deadline(s) stated in the order.

title: Implementing the General Terms of the United States of America-United Kingdom Economic Prosperity Deal
summary: Executive Order 14309 adjusts U.S.–U.K. trade by creating tariff‑rate quotas for automobiles and parts, directing the Secretary of Commerce to amend the Harmonized Tariff Schedule, removing certain aerospace tariffs, and directing future quotas for aluminum and steel articles.
instrument_other_reason: the order adjusts tariff‑rate quotas and tariffs, which is not covered by the listed instrument categories

title: Further Extending the TikTok Enforcement Delay
summary: The order further extends the TikTok enforcement delay until September 17, 2025, and directs the Attorney General to issue guidance and letters.

title: Establishing a White House Office for Special Peace Missions
summary: Executive Order 14311 establishes a new White House Office for Special Peace Missions.

title: Providing for the Revocation of Syria Sanctions
summary: Executive Order 14312 revokes a series of Syria‑related sanctions orders and amends others, while directing agencies to lift sanctions, issue waivers, and take further actions. It expands the national‑emergency authority of EO 13894, amends EO 13606, and references several statutes and prior memoranda.

title: Establishing the President's Make America Beautiful Again Commission
summary: Executive Order 14313 creates the President’s Make America Beautiful Again Commission to advise the President on conservation of natural resources and public lands.

title: Making America Beautiful Again by Improving Our National Parks
summary: Executive Order 14314 directs the Secretary of the Interior (and, where appropriate, the Secretaries of Agriculture and State) to raise non‑resident fees, use the additional revenue for park infrastructure, and review rules; it also revokes a 2017 Presidential Memorandum.

title: Ending Market Distorting Subsidies for Unreliable, Foreign-Controlled Energy Sources
summary: Executive Order 14315 directs the Treasury and Interior secretaries to end federal tax subsidies for wind and solar energy, to review and revise preferential regulations, and to report on actions taken, all within 45‑day time‑frames.

title: Extending the Modification of the Reciprocal Tariff Rates
summary: Executive Order 14316 extends a temporary suspension of tariff duties, keeps an existing PRC suspension unchanged, modifies specific HTSUS headings for a defined period, and delegates implementation authority to senior officials.

title: Creating Schedule G in the Excepted Service
summary: Executive Order 14317 creates a new Schedule G in the excepted service for noncareer positions of a policy‑making or policy‑advocating character. It amends Civil Service Rule VI by adding Schedule G to 5 CFR 6.2 and revises removal provisions in 5 CFR 6.4. The order tasks the Director of the Office of Personnel Management with adopting implementing regulations and directs the Secretary of Veterans Affairs to consider suitability of appointees while prohibiting consideration of political affiliation.

title: Accelerating Federal Permitting of Data Center Infrastructure
summary: Executive Order 14318 directs multiple agencies to accelerate permitting for large‑scale AI data‑center projects and related energy infrastructure. It delegates authority, sets short‑term reporting deadlines, and references existing statutes and programs.

title: Preventing Woke AI in the Federal Government
summary: This order directs federal agencies to procure large language models that adhere to two Unbiased AI Principles—truth‑seeking and ideological neutrality. It tasks the Office of Management and Budget, the Federal Procurement Policy Office, General Services Administration, and the Office of Science and Technology Policy with issuing guidance within 120 days, and requires agency heads to embed compliance terms in contracts and adopt procedures within 90 days. The order references Executive Order 13960 and is grounded in the President’s constitutional and statutory authority.

title: Promoting the Export of the American AI Technology Stack
summary: Executive Order 14320 establishes the American AI Exports Program to promote worldwide export of full‑stack U.S. AI technology, directs the Secretary of Commerce to issue a public call for industry proposals, sets a 90‑day implementation deadline, delegates authority to the SBA Administrator and OSTP Director to appoint members to the Economic Diplomacy Action Group (EDAG), and references several existing statutes and prior presidential actions.

title: Ending Crime and Disorder on America's Streets
summary: The order delegates authority to the Attorney General and several department secretaries to take actions aimed at expanding civil‑commitment and related enforcement measures to address homelessness and public safety.

title: Saving College Sports
summary: Executive Order 14322 directs multiple executive‑branch officials to take actions that preserve and expand college sports, especially women’s and non‑revenue programs, and to prohibit third‑party pay‑for‑play payments.

title: Addressing Threats to the United States by the Government of Brazil
summary: Executive Order 14323 imposes a 40 % ad‑valorem tariff on selected Brazilian products in response to a national emergency caused by actions of the Government of Brazil.

title: Suspending Duty-Free De Minimis Treatment for All Countries
summary: Executive Order 14324 suspends the duty‑free de minimis exemption for virtually all imports and imposes duties on international‑postal shipments, continuing some earlier suspensions and superseding part of EO 14256.

title: Amendment to Duties To Address the Flow of Illicit Drugs Across Our Northern Border
summary: Executive Order 14325 amends the duties imposed on Canadian products, raising the additional ad valorem rate from 25 % to 35 % and establishing a 40 % rate for transshipped goods, and directs the Harmonized Tariff Schedule to be modified accordingly. It delegates authority to the Secretary of Homeland Security, in consultation with Treasury, Commerce, and other agencies, to employ IEEPA powers, publish periodic reports, and monitor the border situation. The order also requires the Secretary of Homeland Security and the Secretary of Commerce to publish a bi‑annual list of circumvention schemes and to continue applying existing stacking‑rule provisions.

title: Further Modifying the Reciprocal Tariff Rates
summary: Executive Order 14326 modifies U.S. tariff rates, imposes additional ad valorem duties on certain foreign trading partners, suspends and later terminates specific HTSUS headings, and directs agencies to monitor and report on the emergency declared in EO 14257.

title: President's Council on Sports, Fitness, and Nutrition, and the Reestablishment of the Presidential Fitness Test
summary: Executive Order 14327 establishes a new President’s Council on Sports, Fitness, and Nutrition and reestablishes the Presidential Fitness Test.

title: Establishing the White House Task Force on the 2028 Summer Olympics
summary: Executive Order 14328 creates a White House Task Force to coordinate the 2028 Summer Olympics, designates its leadership, membership, location, reporting requirements, and termination date.
topic_other_reason: The order concerns coordination of the 2028 Summer Olympics, a subject not covered by the predefined topic list.

title: Addressing Threats to the United States by the Government of the Russian Federation
summary: Executive Order 14329 imposes a 25 % ad valorem duty on articles of India imported into the United States as a sanction related to Russian Federation oil.

title: Democratizing Access to Alternative Assets for 401(k) Investors
summary: Executive Order 14330 directs the Secretary of Labor to review and clarify Department‑of‑Labor guidance on fiduciary duties under ERISA with respect to alternative‑asset investments in 401(k) plans, and directs the SEC to consider regulatory changes to facilitate such investments.

title: Guaranteeing Fair Banking for All Americans
summary: The order directs federal banking regulators and the Small Business Administration to take specific actions to eliminate politicized or unlawful debanking, delegating new responsibilities to those agencies.

title: Improving Oversight of Federal Grantmaking
summary: Key operative directives in Executive Order 14332 (Improving Oversight of Federal Grantmaking)

title: Declaring a Crime Emergency in the District of Columbia
summary: Executive Order 14333 declares a crime emergency in the District of Columbia, directs the Mayor to provide Metropolitan Police services for federal purposes, delegates that authority to the Attorney General, and requires the Attorney General to monitor and report on the emergency.

title: Further Modifying Reciprocal Tariff Rates To Reflect Ongoing Discussions With the People's Republic of China
summary: Executive Order 14334 modifies and temporarily suspends ad valorem duties on imports from the People’s Republic of China, extending a suspension that began under EO 14298.

title: Enabling Competition in the Commercial Space Industry
summary: Executive Order 14335 directs multiple agencies to streamline regulatory processes, create new positions, and produce reports to accelerate the U.S. commercial space industry.
instrument_other_reason: The order contains many distinct directives; each claim below is classified individually.

title: Ensuring American Pharmaceutical Supply Chain Resilience by Filling the Strategic Active Pharmaceutical Ingredients Reserve
summary: Executive Order 14336 directs the Assistant Secretary for Preparedness and Response (ASPR) to develop lists, secure funding, ready the Strategic Active Pharmaceutical Ingredients Reserve (SAPIR), obtain API supplies, and produce plans, each with specific time‑frames.

title: Revocation of Executive Order on Competition
summary: Executive Order 14337 revokes Executive Order 14036, which had promoted competition in the American economy. The order states that it does not impair any existing authority of executive departments, agencies, or the OMB director, and it requires the Department of Justice to cover publication costs. It is to be implemented consistent with applicable law and subject to appropriations.

title: Improving Our Nation Through Better Design
summary: Executive Order 14338 creates a new National Design Studio and a Chief Design Officer, establishes a temporary organization that will end three years after the order, and directs agency heads to deliver initial results by a specific deadline.

title: Additional Measures To Address the Crime Emergency in the District of Columbia
summary: Executive Order 14339 directs multiple federal officials to take actions aimed at addressing a declared crime emergency in the District of Columbia. The order primarily concerns public safety and law‑enforcement matters and delegates authority to various officials to hire personnel, create specialized units, investigate compliance, and conduct inspections.

title: Measures To End Cashless Bail and Enforce the Law in the District of Columbia
summary: Executive Order 14340 directs federal officials to end cashless‑bail policies in the District of Columbia by delegating authority to the Attorney General, agency heads, and task‑force members, while preserving existing agency authority.

title: Prosecuting Burning of the American Flag
summary: Executive Order 14341 directs senior officials to enforce existing criminal and civil statutes against American‑Flag desecration and to use immigration authorities to deny or revoke benefits for foreign nationals who engage in such conduct.

title: Taking Steps To End Cashless Bail To Protect Americans
summary: The order directs the Attorney General to report jurisdictions that have largely eliminated cash bail and requires agency heads to identify federal funds that may be suspended for those jurisdictions.

title: Further Exclusions From the Federal Labor- Management Relations Program
summary: Executive Order 14343 amends Executive Order 12171 to add additional federal agencies to the list of entities excluded from the Federal Labor‑Management Relations Program and extends the filing deadline for related orders issued under EO 14251.

title: Making Federal Architecture Beautiful Again
summary: Executive Order 14344 sets federal‑architecture policy, directs the General Services Administration (GSA) to update its rules, creates a senior‑advisor position, and imposes a 30‑day notice requirement for designs that diverge from the preferred style.

title: Implementing the United States-Japan Agreement
summary: Executive Order 14345 implements the United States‑Japan Agreement by establishing a baseline 15 percent tariff on most Japanese imports, delegating authority to the Secretaries of Commerce and Homeland Security to carry out the order (including publishing required notices within 7 days), and superseding any inconsistent prior proclamations or executive orders.

title: Modifying the Scope of Reciprocal Tariffs and Establishing Procedures for Implementing Trade and Security Agreements
summary: Executive Order 14346 modifies the scope of reciprocal tariffs, updates the Harmonized Tariff Schedule, and delegates implementation authority to the Secretary of Commerce, the Secretary of Homeland Security, and the United States Trade Representative.

title: Restoring the United States Department of War
summary: Executive Order 14347 directs the Secretary of War to provide two reports to the President within specified time‑frames concerning the use of secondary “Department of War” titles and a plan to permanently rename the Department of Defense.

title: Strengthening Efforts To Protect U.S. Nationals From Wrongful Detention Abroad
summary: Executive Order 14348 (2025) authorizes the Secretary of State to label foreign governments that detain U.S. nationals as “State Sponsors of Wrongful Detention,” to impose a suite of sanctions and other restrictive measures against such governments, and to terminate the designation when certain conditions are met.

title: Establishing an Emergency Board To Investigate Disputes Between the Long Island Rail Road Company and Certain of Its Employees Represented by Certain Labor Organizations
summary: Executive Order 14349 establishes an emergency board to investigate and report on labor disputes between the Long Island Rail Road and certain employee unions. The President appoints the board members, the board must submit a report within 30 days, and parties are prohibited from changing dispute conditions for 120 days. Publication costs are assigned to the Department of Transportation and records will be transferred to the National Mediation Board upon termination.

title: Further Extending the TikTok Enforcement Delay
summary: Executive Order 14350 extends the TikTok enforcement delay, directs the Attorney General to issue guidance and a liability‑waiver letter, and confirms the Department of Justice will not enforce the Act during the extended period.

title: The Gold Card
summary: Executive Order 14351 creates the Gold Card visa program, a pathway for foreign investors who donate at least $1 million (or $2 million for corporations) to the United States. The program is overseen by the Secretary of Commerce in coordination with the Secretaries of State and Homeland Security, which must implement the program within 90 days. The order directs the Treasury to hold the gifts in a separate fund and treats the donation as evidence of eligibility for an immigrant visa.

title: Saving TikTok While Protecting National Security
summary: Executive Order 14352 primarily revokes a prior Presidential Memorandum and amends the 2020 Divestment Order while directing the Attorney General to suspend enforcement of the Protecting Americans from Foreign Adversary Controlled Applications Act for a limited period.

title: Assuring the Security of the State of Qatar
summary: The order directs the United States to treat any armed attack on Qatar as a threat to U.S. peace and security, to take diplomatic, economic, and military measures if such an attack occurs, to have the Secretary of War (with the Secretary of State and the Director of National Intelligence) maintain joint contingency planning with Qatar, to have the Secretary of State reaffirm the U.S. security assurance to Qatar and coordinate with allies, to require all federal departments and agencies to implement the order, and to charge the Department of State with publication costs.

title: Continuance of Certain Federal Advisory Committees
summary: Executive Order 14354 continues a list of existing federal advisory committees until 30 September 2027 and supersedes sections 1‑2 of EO 14109.
instrument_other_reason: continues existing advisory committees rather than creating, amending, sanctioning, delegating, reporting, or adjusting pay

title: Unlocking Cures for Pediatric Cancer With Artificial Intelligence
summary: Executive Order 14355 directs existing bodies to use artificial‑intelligence (AI) tools to accelerate pediatric‑cancer research and care, expands federal investment, and sets data‑sharing standards.

title: Ensuring Continued Accountability in Federal Hiring
summary: The order creates agency‑level Strategic Hiring Committees to govern federal hiring.

title: Modifying Duties Addressing the Synthetic Opioid Supply Chain in the People's Republic of China
summary: Executive Order 14357 reduces the additional ad‑valorem duty on certain Chinese‑origin articles from 20 % to 10 % and amends the Harmonized Tariff Schedule accordingly; it directs the Secretary of Homeland Security (and, where appropriate, other officials) to monitor the underlying national‑emergency, to make any further HTSUS changes, and delegates implementation authority.

title: Modifying Reciprocal Tariff Rates Consistent With the Economic and Trade Arrangement Between the United States and the People's Republic of China
summary: Executive Order 14358 modifies tariff policy toward the People’s Republic of China by extending a suspension of heightened reciprocal tariffs, directing agencies to monitor and report on the national‑emergency conditions, and delegating implementation authority to senior officials.
instrument_other_reason: suspends tariff rates and directs agency actions

title: Fostering the Future for American Children and Families
summary: Executive Order 14359 directs the Secretary of Health and Human Services (HHS) to take a series of actions aimed at modernizing the child‑welfare system and expanding opportunities for youth in or leaving foster care.  The order does not create a new body, impose sanctions, or amend prior orders; it primarily **delegates authority** to HHS to carry out the listed tasks.
topic_other_reason: The order’s focus is on children, families and foster‑care services – a subject that falls under the broader civil‑rights/children‑and‑families domain.

title: Modifying the Scope of the Reciprocal Tariffs With Respect to Certain Agricultural Products
summary: Executive Order 14360 modifies the scope of reciprocal tariffs on certain agricultural products, updates the Harmonized Tariff Schedule, delegates implementation authority to senior officials, and attaches updated annexes to prior orders.

title: Modifying the Scope of Tariffs on the Government of Brazil
summary: Executive Order 14361 modifies the United States Harmonized Tariff Schedule to remove certain agricultural products from the additional 40 % ad valorem duty imposed by Executive Order 14323, with the changes effective for goods entered for consumption on or after 12:01 a.m. EST on 13 November 2025. The order updates Annex I to EO 14323 and adds Annex II to this order, and directs the Secretary of State and other senior officials to implement the changes.

title: Designation of Certain Muslim Brotherhood Chapters as Foreign Terrorist Organizations and Specially Designated Global Terrorists
summary: Executive Order 14362 designates certain Muslim Brotherhood chapters as Foreign Terrorist Organizations and Specially Designated Global Terrorists, establishes reporting and action timelines, and clarifies that it creates no enforceable rights.

title: Launching the Genesis Mission
summary: Executive Order 14363 establishes the Genesis Mission, a national effort led by the Department of Energy to accelerate AI‑driven scientific discovery. It tasks the Secretary of Energy with implementing the Mission and the Assistant to the President for Science and Technology with overall leadership, and creates the American Science and Security Platform to support the work. The order sets multiple deadlines for resource identification, data‑asset planning, capability reviews, and reporting to the President.

title: Addressing Security Risks From Price Fixing and Anti-Competitive Behavior in the Food Supply Chain
summary: Executive Order 14364 establishes Food Supply Chain Security Task Forces in the Department of Justice and the Federal Trade Commission and requires them to brief Congress on their progress.

title: Ensuring a National Policy Framework for Artificial Intelligence
summary: Executive Order 14365 creates a new AI Litigation Task Force to challenge State AI laws that conflict with a national AI policy framework.

title: Protecting American Investors From Foreign-Owned and Politically-Motivated Proxy Advisors
summary: Executive Order 14366 directs existing agencies to review, revise, and enforce rules governing proxy advisors, antitrust practices, and fiduciary standards for retirement plans.

title: Designating Fentanyl as a Weapon of Mass Destruction
summary: Executive Order 14367 designates illicit fentanyl and its core precursor chemicals as weapons of mass destruction and delegates a range of enforcement and policy actions to senior officials.

title: Adjustments of Certain Rates of Pay
summary: Executive Order 14368 updates the pay schedules for multiple federal pay systems, sets effective dates for the new schedules, and supersedes the previous order on pay adjustments.

title: Ensuring American Space Superiority
summary: Executive Order 14369 directs the President’s Science and Technology office and other agencies to develop plans, reports and guidance to advance U.S. space policy, including exploration, national security, commercial development and acquisition reforms.

title: Increasing Medical Marijuana and Cannabidiol Research
summary: The order directs the Attorney General to finish rulemaking to move marijuana to Schedule III, tasks the Assistant to the President with revising hemp‑derived cannabinoid product definitions, and requires senior health officials to develop real‑world‑evidence research methods for those products.

title: Providing for the Closing of Executive Departments and Agencies of the Federal Government on December 24, 2025, and December 26, 2025
summary: The order directs the closure of all executive departments and agencies on two specific dates and delegates implementation authority to the Director of the Office of Personnel Management.

title: Prioritizing the Warfighter in Defense Contracting
summary: Executive Order 14372 directs the Secretary of War to prohibit defense contractors from paying dividends or buying back stock, to review contractor performance, and to embed anti‑stock‑buy‑back provisions in future contracts.

title: Safeguarding Venezuelan Oil Revenue for the Good of the American and Venezuelan People
summary: Executive Order 14373 protects Venezuelan‑origin oil revenue held in U.S. Treasury accounts by prohibiting attachment, delegating authority to the Treasury, requiring congressional reporting, and superseding earlier orders.

title: Establishing a Second Emergency Board To Investigate Disputes Between the Long Island Rail Road Company and Certain of Its Employees Represented by Certain Labor Organizations
summary: Executive Order 14374 establishes a second emergency board to investigate Long Island Rail Road labor disputes, sets reporting and procedural deadlines, and assigns record‑keeping and cost responsibilities.

title: Designating the Board of Peace as a Public International Organization Entitled To Enjoy Certain Privileges, Exemptions, and Immunities
summary: Executive Order 14375 designates the Board of Peace as a public international organization entitled to the privileges, exemptions, and immunities provided by the International Organizations Immunities Act.
instrument_other_reason: designates an existing entity to enjoy privileges, exemptions, and immunities; does not create a new body, impose sanctions, revoke/amend, confer a medal, delegate authority, direct a report, or adjust pay.

title: Stopping Wall Street From Competing With Main Street Homebuyers
summary: The order directs multiple federal officials to develop definitions, issue guidance, review and possibly revise rules, conduct antitrust reviews, require ownership disclosures, and prepare legislative recommendations—all aimed at limiting large institutional investors from acquiring single‑family homes that could be bought by families.

title: Addressing State and Local Failures To Rebuild Los Angeles After Wildfire Disasters
summary: Executive Order 14377 directs federal agencies to pre‑empt obstructive state permitting, set tight timelines for rulemaking, expedite environmental waivers, propose legislation, and audit Hazard Mitigation Grant Program funds.

title: Continuance of the Federal Emergency Management Agency Review Council
summary: Executive Order 14378 continues the Federal Emergency Management Agency Review Council, which was originally created by EO 14180, extending its existence until March 25, 2026. The order assigns the Secretary of Homeland Security to perform the Council’s functions under the Federal Advisory Committee Act, following regulations set by the Administrator of General Services. It takes effect on January 24, 2026 and includes standard general provisions.

title: Addressing Addiction Through the Great American Recovery Initiative
summary: The order creates the White House Great American Recovery Initiative to coordinate the federal response to addiction.

title: Addressing Threats to the United States by the Government of Cuba
summary: The order authorizes an additional ad valorem duty on imports of goods that are products of a foreign country that directly or indirectly sells or otherwise provides any oil to Cuba, thereby imposing trade sanctions against those countries.

title: Celebrating American Greatness With American Motor Racing
summary: Executive Order 14381 directs the Secretaries of the Interior and Transportation to plan and enable an INDYCAR street race in Washington, D.C.

title: Addressing Threats to the United States by the Government of Iran
summary: Executive Order 14382 imposes additional tariffs on imports from countries that trade with Iran and delegates implementation authority to senior officials.

title: Establishing an America First Arms Transfer Strategy
summary: Executive Order 14383 establishes a new inter‑agency task force and directs multiple agencies to produce reports, plans and catalogs within specified time‑frames to implement an America‑First arms‑transfer strategy.

title: Modifying Duties To Address Threats to the United States by the Government of the Russian Federation
summary: Executive Order 14384 removes the 25 % ad valorem duty on Indian imports that had been imposed under EO 14329 and terminates the related Harmonized Tariff Schedule headings.

title: Protecting the National Security and Welfare of the United States and Its Citizens From Criminal Actors and Other Public Safety Threats
summary: Executive Order 14385 directs federal officials to share criminal‑history record information (CHRI) with the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) and, under reciprocal agreements, with trusted foreign partners for border‑security and immigration purposes.

title: Strengthening United States National Defense With America's Beautiful Clean Coal Power Generation Fleet
summary: The order directs the Secretary of War, together with the Secretary of Energy, to procure coal‑generated electricity for federal installations through long‑term power purchase agreements.

title: Promoting the National Defense by Ensuring an Adequate Supply of Elemental Phosphorus and Glyphosate- Based Herbicides
summary: The order delegates authority to the Secretary of Agriculture to secure domestic supplies of elemental phosphorus and glyphosate‑based herbicides, requires the Secretary to issue implementing orders and regulations, and confers immunity to domestic producers under the Defense Production Act.

title: Continuing the Suspension of Duty-Free De Minimis Treatment for All Countries
summary: Executive Order 14388 continues the suspension of duty‑free de minimis treatment by amending Executive Order 14324, delegates implementation authority to the Secretary of Homeland Security, and sets an effective date for the modifications.
topic_other_reason: order concerns trade duties and customs rather than any listed subject area

title: Ending Certain Tariff Actions
summary: Executive Order 14389 terminates the additional ad valorem duties imposed under IEEPA by a series of earlier executive orders addressing various national security and foreign policy threats. It directs the heads of all executive departments and agencies to end collection of those duties as soon as practicable and authorizes the Secretaries of Commerce and Homeland Security and the U.S. Trade Representative to modify the Harmonized Tariff Schedule if needed. The order does not affect other duties or related proclamations.

title: Combating Cybercrime, Fraud, and Predatory Schemes Against American Citizens
summary: The order directs senior officials to review relevant frameworks and, within 120 days, submit an action plan that creates an operational cell within the National Coordination Center (NCC).

title: Adjusting Certain Delegations Under the Defense Production Act
summary: The order amends a delegation provision in EO 13603 and clarifies a provision of EO 14156 concerning the Defense Production Act.

title: Ensuring Truthful Advertising of Products Claiming To Be Made in America
summary: Executive Order 14392 directs the Federal Trade Commission and other federal agencies to enforce, regulate, and verify “Made in America” advertising claims, and clarifies that the order does not impair existing agency authority.

title: Promoting Access to Mortgage Credit
summary: Executive Order 14393 directs multiple financial‑regulatory agencies to consider regulatory reforms that reduce burdens on community and smaller banks and to report on housing‑finance market efficiency.
topic_other_reason: The order’s overall focus is on mortgage credit and housing finance, which falls under the administration of federal financial‑regulatory agencies.

title: Removing Regulatory Barriers to Affordable Home Construction
summary: Executive Order 14394 directs multiple federal agencies to review, revise, and streamline regulations, guidance, and programs that increase the cost or delay of residential construction, with a specific 60‑day deadline for HUD to issue best‑practice recommendations for state and local governments.

title: Establishing the Task Force To Eliminate Fraud
summary: Executive Order 14395 creates a new inter‑agency Task Force to eliminate fraud in federal benefit programs.

title: Preserving America's Game
summary: The order directs the Secretary of Commerce and the FCC Chairman to work with the College Football Playoff Committee, the NCAA and other stakeholders to create an exclusive broadcast window for the Army‑Navy Game, preventing any other college football game from being aired at the same time. It also instructs the FCC Chairman to review broadcast licensees' public‑interest obligations to ensure the game remains a national service event. The order cites presidential authority under the Constitution and U.S. law.
topic_other_reason: Preserving the Army‑Navy football game broadcast schedule

title: Further Continuance of the Federal Emergency Management Agency Review Council
summary: The order further continues the Federal Emergency Management Agency Review Council until a specified date and supersedes sections of a prior order.

title: Addressing DEI Discrimination by Federal Contractors
summary: Executive Order 14398 directs federal agencies to embed a clause prohibiting racially discriminatory DEI activities in all contracts, imposes sanctions for non‑compliance, mandates agency‑wide reporting, and requires OMB, the Attorney General, and the Federal Acquisition Regulatory Council to issue guidance and consider enforcement actions.
topic_other_reason: The order primarily concerns procurement and contract administration within the federal government.
instrument_other_reason: The order imposes cancellation, termination, suspension, and debarment of contracts for non‑compliance with the anti‑DEI clause.

title: Ensuring Citizenship Verification and Integrity in Federal Elections
summary: Executive Order 14399 directs federal agencies to verify citizenship of voters, create and transmit state‑level citizenship lists, prioritize investigations of election fraud, and issue USPS rulemaking on ballot envelopes, with specific deadlines and a sanction of withholding funds for non‑compliance.

title: Urgent National Action To Save College Sports
summary: Executive Order 14400 directs multiple federal officials to take actions that regulate college athletics and higher‑education institutions, establishes reporting and compliance requirements, and sets an August 1 2026 deadline for several provisions.

title: Accelerating Medical Treatments for Serious Mental Illness
summary: Executive Order 14401 directs several federal officials and agencies to accelerate the development, review, and access to psychedelic drugs for serious mental illness, and to allocate funding and data‑sharing resources to support this effort.

title: Promoting Efficiency, Accountability, and Performance in Federal Contracting
summary: The order assigns new procurement‑related responsibilities to agency heads, the Director of OMB, and the Administrator for Federal Procurement Policy.

title: Promoting Retirement-Savings Access for American Workers by Establishing TrumpIRA.gov
summary: Executive Order 14403 creates new Treasury‑led responsibilities to launch a retirement‑savings information website and to issue worker‑protection guidance for IRAs.
topic_other_reason: The order’s substantive focus is on retirement‑savings access, which falls under the broader administration of federal programs; no more specific topic label is available in the taxonomy.

title: Imposing Sanctions on Those Responsible for Repression in Cuba and for Threats to United States National Security and Foreign Policy
summary: Executive Order 14404 imposes sanctions on the Government of Cuba, its officials, and related entities by blocking property, restricting travel, and authorizing the Treasury to sanction foreign financial institutions. It directs the Secretaries of State and Treasury to determine sanctionable persons, implement the measures, and report to Congress on the national emergency declared in EO 14380.

title: Integrating Financial Technology Innovation Into Regulatory Frameworks
summary: Executive Order 14405 directs federal financial regulators and the Federal Reserve to review and adjust regulations, conduct studies, and report findings to promote fintech innovation.

title: Restoring Integrity to America's Financial System
summary: Executive Order 14406 directs Treasury, the CFPB, and federal financial regulators to take a series of actions aimed at protecting the U.S. financial system from illicit activity and credit‑risk exposure associated with non‑work‑authorized individuals.

title: Realigning United States Core Childhood Vaccine Recommendations With Best Practices From Peer, Developed Countries
summary: Executive Order 14407 directs the CDC and its Advisory Committee on Immunization Practices to review a scientific assessment and, as permitted by law, update the United States childhood and adolescent vaccine schedule. It requires every executive department and agency to align their immunization actions, regulations, funding, and coverage with the updated schedule and to maintain cost‑free coverage through private insurance, Medicaid, CHIP, and the Vaccines for Children Program. The HHS Director of the Office of Intergovernmental and External Affairs must inform state officials of the order’s policies and make the scientific assessment available for state vaccination law considerations.

title: Removing Unnecessary and Counterproductive Restrictions on Access to Federal Lands
summary: Executive Order 14408 rescinds two prior orders that regulated off‑road vehicle use on federal lands and directs the relevant secretaries and agencies to begin rulemakings to repeal or revise the regulations that implemented those orders.

title: Promoting Advanced Artificial Intelligence Innovation and Security
summary: Executive Order 14409 directs multiple federal officials to prioritize cyber‑defense of government systems, create an AI‑cybersecurity clearinghouse, and develop a framework for “covered frontier” AI models. The order’s first‑listed action is the creation of a new body, so the overall primary topic is technology_and_research and the instrument is creates_body.

title: Implementing Schedule Policy/Career in the Excepted Service
summary: Executive Order 14410 amends civil‑service regulations, directs agency actions, and creates award and reporting requirements related to the new Schedule Policy/Career in the excepted service.

title: Strengthening Customs Enforcement
summary: Executive Order 14411 directs the Secretary of Homeland Security to take a series of actions to strengthen U.S. customs enforcement.  The order delegates authority to the Secretary to revise regulations, impose new requirements on importers of record, enhance vetting, increase penalties, improve transparency, and report on progress.

title: Securing the Nation Against Advanced Cryptographic Attacks
summary: Executive Order 14412 directs federal agencies to transition to post‑quantum cryptography (PQC) and establishes coordination, reporting, and procurement actions to achieve that transition.

title: Ushering in the Next Frontier of Quantum Innovation
summary: Executive Order 14413 directs a whole‑of‑government effort to accelerate quantum information science and technology (QIST) across research, manufacturing, commercialization, and national security. It creates the Quantum Computer for Application Development and Discovery Science (QC‑ADDS) Effort, updates the National Quantum Strategy, and mandates multiple agencies to develop plans, reports, and workforce initiatives to secure U.S. leadership in quantum innovation. The order also reconstitutes the National Quantum Initiative Advisory Committee and sets a series of deadlines for strategy updates, reports, and partnership models.

title: Advancing Regenerative Agriculture and Strengthening American Farm Resilience
summary: Executive Order 14414 directs federal agencies to prioritize registration of alternative agricultural substances, develop chemical‑exposure research frameworks, launch a NIH grand‑prize challenge, expand the Regenerative Pilot Program, and sets implementation and cost‑bearing rules.

title: Securing America's Defense Supply Chains and Ensuring Domestic Acquisition of Critical Materials
summary: Executive Order 14415 directs the Secretary of War (and other department secretaries) to tighten domestic‑source requirements for defense‑critical materials, to map and illuminate supply chains, to develop regulations and qualification strategies, and to report on progress.  The order primarily concerns national‑security supply‑chain resilience and delegates authority to the Secretary of War to carry out these actions.

title: Restoring Trust in the Smithsonian Institution
summary: The order directs several senior officials to identify and use any authorities they have to carry out the order’s policy, effectively delegating authority to them.

title: Establishing the President's Military Spouse Commission
summary: Establishes the President's Military Spouse Commission, a body to advise the President on policies affecting military spouses and families.

title: Continuing To Protect the Meaning and Value of American Citizenship
summary: Executive Order 14418 directs federal departments and agencies not to issue or accept documents recognizing United States citizenship for persons whose parents are alien enemies, foreign government employees, or who engage in birthright citizenship transactions. It delegates authority to the Secretary of State, Attorney General, Secretary of Homeland Security, and Commissioner of Social Security to ensure departmental policies comply, and requires heads of all executive departments and agencies to issue public guidance within 30 days. The order cites the International Emergency Economic Powers Act and 8 U.S.C. 1189 as legal authorities.

title: Ending Birth Tourism
summary: The order defines birth tourism, delegates authority to the Secretaries of State and Homeland Security to implement measures preventing entry, revoking visas, and allowing humanitarian or national‑interest exemptions.

title: Delivering Gold Standard Childhood Vaccine Recommendations for Americans
summary: Executive Order 14420 establishes Gold Standard Childhood Vaccine Recommendations and directs federal agencies to review them, tasks the HHS Secretary and Task Force to present implementation plans within 90 days, and orders the Attorney General and the Departments of Justice, Education, and HHS to protect parental choice and religious exemptions in state vaccination laws.

title: Declaring a National Emergency To Secure the United States Bulk-Power System
summary: Executive Order 14421 declares a national emergency concerning the United States bulk‑power system and prohibits the acquisition, importation, transfer, or installation of foreign‑produced bulk‑power system electric equipment, directing the Secretary of Energy to issue rules and procurement recommendations.

title: Honoring the American History of the Great Lakes and Renaming Lake Ontario as Lake America
summary: Executive Order 14422 directs the Secretary of the Interior to rename Lake Ontario as “Lake America” and sets a 30‑day deadline for completing the renaming.

title: Establishing the United States Space Academy
summary: Executive Order 14423 establishes a presidential commission to develop a United States Space Academy and directs the commission to submit a report within 120 days.
